standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the base cases of the two inductions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Relative and absolute Mayer-Vietoris sequences
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the relative Mayer-Vietoris sequence for a morphism and the Mayer-Vietoris sequence for the cohomology of a scheme
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the induction steps, since a bound valid for U, V and U cap V propagates to X = U union V.

core_obligations: Prove (1) by induction (proof lines 20051-20060): assume Y affine and use the induction principle; if X is affine the bound holds by the affine base case, and if X = U union V with the statement known for U -> Y, V -> Y and U cap V -> Y then the relative Mayer-Vietoris sequence propagates the finite bound to X.

Prove (2) by induction (proof lines 20062-20070): use the induction principle again; the affine case is the cited bound for affine schemes over a field of finite cohomological dimension, and the Mayer-Vietoris sequence propagates the bound from U, V and U cap V to X.
proof_roadmap: Reduce each assertion to the affine case, quoting the corresponding bound.
Propagate the bound along X = U union V using the appropriate Mayer-Vietoris sequence.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a field K, every finite type morphism of K-schemes has finite cohomological dimension, and that if K itself has finite cohomological dimension then so does every finite type K-scheme (statement lines 20040-20049). The proof (proof lines 20051-20071) runs the induction principle twice: once with the affine base case and the relative Mayer-Vietoris sequence, and once with the affine bound and the absolute Mayer-Vietoris sequence. H2: two parallel inductive arguments, written out in full.
